subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: In an integrated crop-livestock system, recycling crop residues as animal feed most directly creates which linkage?
options: A separation of crop and livestock nutrient cycles
A substitution of biological inputs by only mineral inputs
A nutrient-and-biomass flow between crop and livestock enterprises
A conversion of all crop land to permanent pasture
explanation: A nutrient-and-biomass flow between crop and livestock enterprises [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: A farm plan that allocates scarce irrigation water first to stages with greatest yield sensitivity is applying the principle of:
explanation: Efficient resource allocation [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: In a crop-livestock system, manure is primarily valuable as a source of:
explanation: Organic matter and plant nutrients [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: Which is the best example of biological resource management?
options: Using crop varieties, livestock breeds and beneficial organisms suited to farm objectives
explanation: Using crop varieties, livestock breeds and beneficial organisms suited to farm objectives [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: Which action most clearly improves water-use efficiency at farm level?
options: Maintaining irrigation regardless of soil moisture
Delivering water closer to crop demand while reducing conveyance and application losses
explanation: Delivering water closer to crop demand while reducing conveyance and application losses [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: Which management choice best integrates biological and environmental resources?
options: Using identical varieties in every agro-ecological zone
Selecting crop species and rotations suited to local soil and climate
Treating soil as independent of biological processes
explanation: Selecting crop species and rotations suited to local soil and climate [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: A farm that combines annual crops with nitrogen-fixing trees to improve nutrient cycling is using:
options: Biological integration of enterprises and species
explanation: Biological integration of enterprises and species [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: Which farm by-product is commonly suitable for recycling through ruminants?
explanation: Cereal straw [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: Why are legumes often important in integrated crop rotations?
options: They eliminate the need for phosphorus and water
They can add biologically fixed nitrogen and diversify the rotation
They always require more nitrogen fertilizer than cereals
explanation: They can add biologically fixed nitrogen and diversify the rotation [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: A principal advantage of enterprise diversification in an integrated farm is that it can:
options: Guarantee identical returns from all enterprises
Remove the need for farm management decisions
Spread production and income risk across enterprises
explanation: Spread production and income risk across enterprises [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: Which practice best represents resource complementarity in integrated agriculture?
options: Burning crop residues before every sowing
Using livestock manure to improve soil fertility in crop fields
Keeping livestock and crop nutrient cycles completely separate
Replacing all on-farm feed with imported concentrate
explanation: Using livestock manure to improve soil fertility in crop fields [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: Which situation indicates inefficient energy use in agriculture?
options: Matching tractor power to implement requirement
Maintaining machinery to reduce fuel loss
High fuel consumption per unit of useful field operation due to poorly matched machinery
explanation: High fuel consumption per unit of useful field operation due to poorly matched machinery [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: Farm-resource integration is strongest when:
options: Enterprises are planned independently of each other
By-products are discarded regardless of value
Every enterprise purchases all inputs externally
The output or by-product of one enterprise becomes an input to another
explanation: The output or by-product of one enterprise becomes an input to another [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: A key reason for integrating enterprises on small farms is to:
options: Use labour, land and by-products more continuously through the year
Ensure all labour is needed on the same day
explanation: Use labour, land and by-products more continuously through the year [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: The systems approach to agriculture differs from single-enterprise analysis because it emphasizes:
options: Interactions, trade-offs and flows among farm components
Only the yield of one crop in isolation
Only the purchase price of machinery
Only annual rainfall totals without farm response
explanation: Interactions, trade-offs and flows among farm components [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: Which criterion is most appropriate for judging “efficient utilization” of a scarce farm resource?
options: Greater useful output or value per unit of the limiting resource
Maximum input use regardless of output
explanation: Greater useful output or value per unit of the limiting resource [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: Which outcome is most consistent with efficient nutrient recycling on a mixed farm?
options: Permanent separation of manure from cropland
Higher nutrient leakage from the farm
Lower nutrient losses and reduced dependence on external nutrient inputs
explanation: Lower nutrient losses and reduced dependence on external nutrient inputs [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: Which resource is converted by photosynthesis into chemical energy stored in crop biomass?
explanation: Solar radiation [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: The productive capacity of agricultural land is most directly constrained by which land-resource attribute?
options: Soil depth, fertility and physical condition
explanation: Soil depth, fertility and physical condition [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: Which statement best distinguishes a mixed farming system from a specialized crop farm?
options: Mixed farming excludes animals from the farm
Mixed farming is defined only by farm size
Mixed farming necessarily means rainfed farming
Mixed farming deliberately combines crop and livestock enterprises on the same farm system
explanation: Mixed farming deliberately combines crop and livestock enterprises on the same farm system [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: In integrated farming, “circularity” is most closely associated with:
options: Growing a single crop continuously for market specialization
Reusing by-products and nutrients among farm enterprises
Separating waste streams from productive use
explanation: Reusing by-products and nutrients among farm enterprises [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: In resource accounting, crop residues fed to livestock should be viewed primarily as:
options: A farm resource with an alternative productive use
explanation: A farm resource with an alternative productive use [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: Integration of trees, crops and livestock on the same land-management unit is most closely associated with:
explanation: Agroforestry-based integrated production [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: In integrated agriculture, livestock can contribute to crop production most directly through:
options: Manure, traction in some systems, and use of crop by-products
explanation: Manure, traction in some systems, and use of crop by-products [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 1. Integrated Agriculture and Efficient Resource Use
question: Which combination most directly reflects the natural-resource base of agriculture?
options: Land, water, biological resources and solar energy
explanation: Land, water, biological resources and solar energy [A03]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: The most defensible basis for releasing an improved variety is:
options: High yield in one pot regardless of target environment
Consistent evidence that it meets defined performance, quality and adaptation criteria through appropriate testing
A novel name without comparative testing
Superiority in a single unreplicated observation only
explanation: Consistent evidence that it meets defined performance, quality and adaptation criteria through appropriate testing [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: Heterosis refers to:
options: Loss of vigour caused by selfing only
Transfer of cytoplasm without nuclear genes
Superior performance of a hybrid relative to its parents for a trait under a defined comparison
explanation: Superior performance of a hybrid relative to its parents for a trait under a defined comparison [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: Specific combining ability refers mainly to:
options: Mean performance of a parent across all crosses
Performance of a particular parental combination beyond what general combining ability predicts
explanation: Performance of a particular parental combination beyond what general combining ability predicts [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: Mutation breeding seeks useful genetic variation by:
options: Selecting environmental modifications that are not inherited
Inducing mutations and selecting desirable heritable variants
explanation: Inducing mutations and selecting desirable heritable variants [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: In a backcross programme, the recurrent parent is the parent that:
options: Is crossed repeatedly to recover most of its genetic background
Contributes the target gene only and is used once
Is never used after the initial cross
Must always be a wild species
explanation: Is crossed repeatedly to recover most of its genetic background [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: Physical mutagens used in mutation breeding include:
options: Ionizing radiation such as gamma rays
explanation: Ionizing radiation such as gamma rays [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: A doubled-haploid line is valuable to breeders because it can achieve:
explanation: Complete or near-complete homozygosity rapidly [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: Marker-assisted selection is most useful when a DNA marker is:
options: Used without any validation in the breeding population
Known only after harvest with no genetic association
Closely linked to or predictive of a target gene/QTL and can improve selection efficiency
explanation: Closely linked to or predictive of a target gene/QTL and can improve selection efficiency [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: A cultivar specifically bred for resistance to a pathogen reduces crop loss by altering:
options: Host susceptibility within the disease interaction
Pathogen population size without host genetics
explanation: Host susceptibility within the disease interaction [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: Phenotypic selection is most efficient for a trait when the trait has:
options: Extremely low heritability with strong environmental noise
High heritability and reliable phenotypic expression
explanation: High heritability and reliable phenotypic expression [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: The principal reason breeders maintain genetic variability in early generations is to:
options: Preserve selectable differences from which favourable recombinants can be identified
Ensure every plant is genetically identical immediately
explanation: Preserve selectable differences from which favourable recombinants can be identified [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: Participatory plant breeding differs from strictly centralized breeding by:
options: Involving farmers/users directly in selection and evaluation, often in target environments
Using only molecular markers and no field testing
Excluding end users from all stages
explanation: Involving farmers/users directly in selection and evaluation, often in target environments [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: Inbreeding depression is most evident in many cross-pollinated species because inbreeding:
options: Prevents any change in genotype frequencies
Increases homozygosity and can expose deleterious recessive alleles
explanation: Increases homozygosity and can expose deleterious recessive alleles [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: Genotype × environment interaction is present when:
options: A trait has no environmental component
Relative performance of genotypes changes across environments
All genotypes respond identically in every environment
Only the environment changes but genotype rankings are invariant by definition
explanation: Relative performance of genotypes changes across environments [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: General combining ability is associated chiefly with:
options: Average performance of a parent in hybrid combinations, largely reflecting additive gene effects
Performance in one specific cross only
explanation: Average performance of a parent in hybrid combinations, largely reflecting additive gene effects [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: For a simply inherited recessive trait introduced by backcrossing, marker-assisted foreground selection can be useful because it:
options: Makes the donor genome identical to the recurrent parent in one cross
Eliminates the need for a recurrent parent
Identifies carriers/target alleles without waiting for difficult phenotypic expression
explanation: Identifies carriers/target alleles without waiting for difficult phenotypic expression [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: Backcross breeding is particularly suited to:
options: Transferring one or a few specific genes into an otherwise desirable recurrent-parent background
Creating maximum genome-wide recombination with no preferred parent
explanation: Transferring one or a few specific genes into an otherwise desirable recurrent-parent background [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: The bulk method in self-pollinated crops differs from the pedigree method because early segregating generations are:
options: Advanced largely as populations with less individual pedigree recording
Backcrossed each generation to the same parent
explanation: Advanced largely as populations with less individual pedigree recording [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: Mass selection differs from pure-line selection because mass selection typically:
options: Selects many superior plants and bulks their progeny rather than tracing a single homozygous line
Requires backcrossing to one recurrent parent in every cycle
explanation: Selects many superior plants and bulks their progeny rather than tracing a single homozygous line [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: Recurrent selection is designed primarily to:
options: Fix a single homozygous line in one generation
Increase the frequency of favourable alleles in a population through repeated cycles of selection and recombination
explanation: Increase the frequency of favourable alleles in a population through repeated cycles of selection and recombination [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: The breeder’s equation R = h2S expresses response to selection (R) as a function of:
options: Only environmental variance and mutation rate
Narrow interpretation here: heritability and selection differential
explanation: Narrow interpretation here: heritability and selection differential [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: A pure-line variety is most closely associated with:
options: A clonal mixture of unrelated genotypes
A highly homozygous line derived through selfing and selection in a self-pollinated crop
A first-generation hybrid maintained by random mating
explanation: A highly homozygous line derived through selfing and selection in a self-pollinated crop [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: Selection response for a quantitative trait depends importantly on:
options: Only plot size regardless of genetic variance
Heritable genetic variation and selection intensity/accuracy
explanation: Heritable genetic variation and selection intensity/accuracy [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: The fundamental objective of plant breeding is to:
options: Change only the appearance of harvested seed without genetic change
Produce identical genotypes for every agro-ecological zone regardless of objective
Eliminate all environmental effects on phenotype
Develop plant populations or varieties with heritable combinations of traits useful for defined environments and users
explanation: Develop plant populations or varieties with heritable combinations of traits useful for defined environments and users [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 10. Plant Breeding and Genetic Improvement of Crops
question: Pedigree selection following a cross is characterized by:
options: Random bulking without any family records or selection
Selection in segregating generations while maintaining ancestry records
Selection only after complete homozygosity with no record of ancestry
Repeated crossing only to a recurrent parent
explanation: Selection in segregating generations while maintaining ancestry records [A08]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: In a formal seed multiplication chain, breeder/foundation/certified classes are used primarily to:
options: Replace germination testing with yield testing only
Maintain genetic identity and quality while multiplying seed to commercial quantities
explanation: Maintain genetic identity and quality while multiplying seed to commercial quantities [A10]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: Seed genetic purity refers to:
options: The degree to which seed is true to the stated variety or genetic identity
explanation: The degree to which seed is true to the stated variety or genetic identity [A10]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: A principal environmental concern considered in GM crop risk assessment is:
options: Potential gene flow/outcrossing to compatible relatives or other crops
Whether the crop contains any DNA at all
explanation: Potential gene flow/outcrossing to compatible relatives or other crops [A09]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: The most appropriate comparison in compositional assessment of a GM food is generally with:
options: An appropriate conventional counterpart and known natural variation
A soil sample from the field
explanation: An appropriate conventional counterpart and known natural variation [A09]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: Seed processing commonly includes cleaning, grading and treatment mainly to:
options: Improve physical quality, uniformity and storability/plantability of the seed lot
explanation: Improve physical quality, uniformity and storability/plantability of the seed lot [A10]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: Seed certification is best described as:
options: An officially controlled system intended to maintain varietal identity and prescribed seed-quality standards through multiplication
A process that tests only seed colour
A guarantee of maximum yield in every field
explanation: An officially controlled system intended to maintain varietal identity and prescribed seed-quality standards through multiplication [A10]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: According to WHO, safety assessment of GM foods should be conducted:
options: By assuming all GM foods are identical
Only on the basis of crop yield
explanation: On a case-by-case basis [A09]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: The most important reason seed storage conditions are species-specific is that:
options: Only seed size determines storage behaviour
Seeds differ in desiccation tolerance, dormancy and physiological response to temperature/moisture
Storage is unrelated to seed moisture
explanation: Seeds differ in desiccation tolerance, dormancy and physiological response to temperature/moisture [A10]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: A selectable marker in plant transformation is used primarily to:
options: Identify cells that have successfully received the transformation construct
Control field weeds after crop establishment
explanation: Identify cells that have successfully received the transformation construct [A09]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: For orthodox seeds, reducing moisture content and storage temperature generally:
options: Extends storage life within species-appropriate limits
Converts orthodox seeds to recalcitrant seeds
Has no effect on deterioration rate
explanation: Extends storage life within species-appropriate limits [A10]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: Recalcitrant seeds differ from orthodox seeds because recalcitrant seeds generally:
options: Remain viable indefinitely at room temperature
Do not tolerate substantial drying and low-temperature storage in the same way
Require extreme drying for long storage
explanation: Do not tolerate substantial drying and low-temperature storage in the same way [A10]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: Isolation distance in seed production is imposed mainly to:
options: Reduce unwanted pollen flow or mechanical admixture and preserve genetic purity
explanation: Reduce unwanted pollen flow or mechanical admixture and preserve genetic purity [A10]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: Gene stacking in crop biotechnology means:
options: Repeating one gene sequence without a trait objective
Combining two or more transgenic/engineered traits in one cultivar or hybrid
Growing two crops in alternate rows
explanation: Combining two or more transgenic/engineered traits in one cultivar or hybrid [A09]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: Seed vigour describes:
options: Properties determining potential for rapid, uniform emergence and development under a range of conditions
explanation: Properties determining potential for rapid, uniform emergence and development under a range of conditions [A10]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: Herbicide-tolerant GM crops are designed primarily to:
options: Produce herbicides in the harvested grain by definition
Survive application of specified herbicides used for weed control
Eliminate all non-target plants without management
explanation: Survive application of specified herbicides used for weed control [A09]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: Which trait has been widely introduced into GM crops to reduce damage from certain insect pests?
options: Permanent tolerance to all abiotic stresses
Expression of insecticidal proteins such as Bt traits
Complete elimination of weeds without herbicides
explanation: Expression of insecticidal proteins such as Bt traits [A09]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: Seed viability is broader than immediate germination performance because viability concerns whether seed is:
options: Alive and capable of germination under suitable conditions, including where dormancy may prevent immediate germination
explanation: Alive and capable of germination under suitable conditions, including where dormancy may prevent immediate germination [A10]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: A standard germination test estimates:
options: The proportion of fertilizer dissolved in soil
The proportion of seeds capable of producing normal seedlings under prescribed favourable conditions
Only field emergence under every stress environment
explanation: The proportion of seeds capable of producing normal seedlings under prescribed favourable conditions [A10]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: Roguing in a seed-production field means:
options: Applying a herbicide to every plant
Removing off-types and undesirable plants before they contaminate the seed crop
explanation: Removing off-types and undesirable plants before they contaminate the seed crop [A10]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: WHO specifically notes allergenicity assessment because transfer of a gene from a commonly allergenic source may:
options: Introduce a protein requiring evaluation for allergenic potential
Remove all proteins from the crop
Change only seed colour with no protein expression
explanation: Introduce a protein requiring evaluation for allergenic potential [A09]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: Why is representative sampling essential in seed testing?
options: Seed tests do not depend on the submitted sample
Laboratory results can characterize the lot only if the submitted sample represents the lot
A larger laboratory always eliminates sampling error
explanation: Laboratory results can characterize the lot only if the submitted sample represents the lot [A10]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: A genetically modified crop is one in which genetic material has been altered using:
options: Modern biotechnology techniques beyond conventional crossing alone
Only selection among existing plants without genetic intervention
explanation: Modern biotechnology techniques beyond conventional crossing alone [A09]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: High seed moisture during storage generally increases the risk of:
options: Rapid deterioration, respiration and storage fungi/insects under suitable conditions
Lower metabolic activity in every species
explanation: Rapid deterioration, respiration and storage fungi/insects under suitable conditions [A10]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: The term “event” in commercial GM crop regulation commonly refers to:
options: A conventional cross between two cultivars
A specific genetic transformation insertion occurrence in a plant genome
explanation: A specific genetic transformation insertion occurrence in a plant genome [A09]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 11. GMO Crops and Seed Production Technology
question: Seed physical purity testing determines the proportion of:
options: Pure seed, other crop/weed seeds and inert matter in a sample
explanation: Pure seed, other crop/weed seeds and inert matter in a sample [A10]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: A windbreak in landscape or farm design should generally be oriented to:
options: Eliminate all vegetation on the windward side
Run parallel to prevailing damaging winds in all cases
explanation: Intercept prevailing damaging winds [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: In protected horticulture, greenhouse production modifies the crop microclimate chiefly by controlling some combination of:
explanation: Temperature, radiation, humidity and ventilation [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: Budding differs from conventional scion grafting chiefly because budding uses:
options: A single bud as the scion unit
A whole rooted plant as scion
explanation: A single bud as the scion unit [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: A major advantage of vegetative propagation of a selected cultivar is:
options: Creation of a new species each generation
Maintenance of the desired genotype as a clone
explanation: Maintenance of the desired genotype as a clone [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: Horticulture conventionally includes intensive cultivation of:
options: Fruits, vegetables, flowers and ornamental plants
explanation: Fruits, vegetables, flowers and ornamental plants [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: A nursery’s primary horticultural function is to:
options: Raise and manage planting material until suitable for field establishment or sale
Operate only as a fertilizer warehouse
explanation: Raise and manage planting material until suitable for field establishment or sale [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: Mulching around horticultural plants can simultaneously:
options: Eliminate the need for drainage under all conditions
Reduce evaporation, moderate soil temperature and suppress weeds
explanation: Reduce evaporation, moderate soil temperature and suppress weeds [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: A stem cutting becomes an independent plant after it develops:
options: Adventitious roots and new shoot growth
explanation: Adventitious roots and new shoot growth [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: In grafting, the scion is:
options: The wound tissue formed after union
The shoot piece of the desired cultivar joined to the rootstock
explanation: The shoot piece of the desired cultivar joined to the rootstock [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: A climacteric fruit is distinguished by:
options: A characteristic rise in respiration and ethylene associated with ripening
An inability to ripen after harvest in all cases
explanation: A characteristic rise in respiration and ethylene associated with ripening [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: Hardening-off nursery plants before transplanting is intended to:
options: Maintain permanently high humidity and low light
Acclimatize them gradually to more stressful field conditions
Prevent any exposure to outdoor conditions
explanation: Acclimatize them gradually to more stressful field conditions [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: Layering produces roots on a stem while it is:
options: Grafted to an unrelated rootstock before rooting
Still attached to the parent plant
explanation: Still attached to the parent plant [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: Training a fruit tree refers mainly to:
options: Removing only diseased tissue regardless of form
Directing plant form and framework, especially when young
explanation: Directing plant form and framework, especially when young [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: Self-incompatibility in a fruit crop can require orchard design that includes:
options: Compatible pollinizer cultivars and pollinating agents
Vegetative propagation as a substitute for fruit set in the orchard
Only one clone with no compatible pollen source
explanation: Compatible pollinizer cultivars and pollinating agents [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: The principal reason for using a compatible rootstock is to combine scion fruit quality with rootstock traits such as:
options: Adaptation, vigour control or resistance to certain soil-borne constraints
Atmospheric nitrogen fixation by all fruit species
explanation: Adaptation, vigour control or resistance to certain soil-borne constraints [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: Floriculture is concerned chiefly with:
options: Flowering and ornamental plants for aesthetic/commercial use
explanation: Flowering and ornamental plants for aesthetic/commercial use [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: Olericulture deals primarily with:
explanation: Vegetable crops [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 12. Horticulture, Floriculture, Propagation and Landscaping
question: Asexual or vegetative propagation produces new plants from:
options: Vegetative organs or tissues rather than seeds formed by sexual reproduction
explanation: Vegetative organs or tissues rather than seeds formed by sexual reproduction [A11]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry

question: The universal soil-loss equation (USLE) was developed to estimate primarily:
options: Gully volume from individual storms only
Long-term average sheet and rill erosion by water
explanation: Long-term average sheet and rill erosion by water [A07]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 9. Soil Erosion, Waterlogging and Salinity Management
question: Saltation in wind erosion refers to:
options: Downslope movement of saturated soil mass
Dissolved salt movement in drainage water
Short bouncing movement of soil particles near the surface
Long-distance suspension of only clay colloids
explanation: Short bouncing movement of soil particles near the surface [A07]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 9. Soil Erosion, Waterlogging and Salinity Management
question: A saline soil is distinguished from a sodic soil mainly by the fact that a sodic soil has:
options: Necessarily lower pH than all saline soils
No infiltration problems under any conditions
Excess exchangeable sodium that can severely impair soil structure
Only soluble salts with no sodium effect on exchange sites
explanation: Excess exchangeable sodium that can severely impair soil structure [A07]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 9. Soil Erosion, Waterlogging and Salinity Management
question: Sheet erosion by water is characterized by:
options: Relatively uniform removal of a thin layer of soil from the land surface
Wind-driven bouncing of sand grains only
Deep, narrow channels that cannot be removed by normal tillage
explanation: Relatively uniform removal of a thin layer of soil from the land surface [A07]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 9. Soil Erosion, Waterlogging and Salinity Management
question: Which management combination is most appropriate for saline-irrigated agriculture?
options: Sensitive crops, no drainage and maximum surface evaporation
Sodic amendment with sodium salts only
Salt-tolerant crops, suitable irrigation water management, leaching and adequate drainage
Permanent deficit irrigation regardless of salt balance
explanation: Salt-tolerant crops, suitable irrigation water management, leaching and adequate drainage [A07]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 9. Soil Erosion, Waterlogging and Salinity Management
question: The principal direct effect of prolonged waterlogging on most upland crops is:
options: Permanent conversion of nitrate into phosphate
Immediate elimination of all soil microbes
Oxygen deficiency in the root zone
explanation: Oxygen deficiency in the root zone [A07]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 9. Soil Erosion, Waterlogging and Salinity Management
question: The most effective way to reduce erosion on sloping cultivated land is generally to:
options: Cultivate directly up and down the steepest slope
Reduce runoff velocity and protect the soil surface
Remove all crop residues before rainfall
Keep soil bare during erosive storms
explanation: Reduce runoff velocity and protect the soil surface [A07]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 9. Soil Erosion, Waterlogging and Salinity Management
question: Capillary rise from a shallow saline water table can worsen surface salinity because:
options: Water evaporates and leaves dissolved salts behind
Capillary rise removes all salts from the profile
explanation: Water evaporates and leaves dissolved salts behind [A07]

subject: Agriculture & Forestry
topic: 9. Soil Erosion, Waterlogging and Salinity Management
question: The standard reclamation principle for a saline soil with adequate drainage is to:
options: Leach soluble salts below the root zone
Concentrate salts at the soil surface
Apply sodium carbonate to increase exchangeable sodium
explanation: Leach soluble salts below the root zone [A07]
